turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have about twenty minutes. Who decided on the zero, and did anyone speak to Owen before it went in?
Before anything else: I entered the zero before I called you. That broke procedure 4.2, and I am sorry Owen found out on his phone.
Okay. What do you have on the essay itself?
Here is the version history. Created Wednesday, October 28, 11:31 PM, title only. At 11:52 PM, 612 words in one edit. At 11:58 PM, 794 more. No earlier drafts. Turn the screen and read it yourself.
People write in one place and paste into another. You still haven't told me who decided on the zero.
If he drafted it somewhere else, that file has its own dates. Bring it and I will look at it with you. Until then, this is the only history there is.
Okay. Whatever else happens, nothing goes on his record and none of this gets said in front of his class. What exactly are you proposing, Hale?
Second: the essay quotes Act 3, Scene 2: The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile. Here is the whole play on my screen. Search every edition you like; the line is not in Hamlet.
Students misremember lines all the time, Hale. A bad quotation is a bad quotation, not a finding about who wrote it.
It is not a misremembered line. There is no line in the play close to it. Search the word exile yourself.

Fine. I'll take a supervised rewrite to put this behind him, but it's private, not in front of his class, and you put in writing tonight that nothing goes on his file. Send it to me and copy the principal.
Third: his in-class writing from September 24. 380 words in 40 minutes, comma splices, no quotations. The essay has nine quotations cited by act, scene and line. Here are both, side by side.
Forty minutes under a clock isn't a weekend at a desk, and anyone's writing changes between the two. I've given you my terms, Hale. In writing tonight, with the principal copied.

Under procedure 4.4 this is a first concern. A supervised rewrite, private, not in front of his class. If it shows the learning, its mark replaces the zero and nothing goes on his record. I will put that in writing tonight.
That's the deal. In writing tonight, the zero withdrawn from the gradebook the moment you send it, and I want the date for the rewrite in the same email.
Will he do it?
He'll be there. Put the date and the time in the email, Hale.
END MEETING

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Cc: the principal

Hale,

You agreed in our meeting that Owen will complete a supervised rewrite, privately and not in front of his class, that its mark will replace the zero, and that nothing will go on his record. I still want the zero removed from the gradebook and the date and time of the rewrite in the same email. You said you would put this in writing tonight, and I expect it then.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: She reached her last position and agreed to a private supervised rewrite whose mark replaces the zero, with nothing on his record, and she still wants that in writing, the zero off the gradebook, and a date and time; that is the fair outcome under procedure 4.4, and her time did not run out.
What moved her: You answered each of her defences with something she could check herself, first the version history and then the line that does not exist in the play, so she had nothing left to push against.
What cost ground: Nothing; you owned entering the zero before calling home in one sentence and did not defend it.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM, saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, watched Owen close it, and never asked; your version history, with its edits just before midnight the night before the due date, came close to that, which is why she got shorter and went straight to procedure, and it proves nothing about the essay, it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: When she asked who decided on the zero, answer it directly the first time, since she came back to it twice before you did.
